prompt: Can you check what workspace role Robert has? He's a member of the channel where the team's been talking through AI model work — I just need his membership role in our workspace.
binding_note: The route runs WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP -> WORKSPACE -> CONVERSATION -> CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP: the workspace membership belongs to the same user who holds a conversation membership in a channel hosting AI-model-work discussion within that workspace. 'Robert' plus the vague channel descriptor is genuinely underspecified: 'engineering' (topic 'Engineering Team', hosting circuit-tracer/PyTorch interpretability threads) has member Robert Walsh, while 'model-research' (topic 'Model training, evals, papers, architectures') has member Robert Chen — both are ordinary AI-model-work channels and both members are literally named Robert, giving two distinct possible referent sets for the same workspace-membership request.

obligations.name: robert_workspace_role_lookup
obligations.description: Select the workspace-membership record (user_teams row) for the user named Robert who holds a conversation membership in the channel where the team discusses AI model work; report that user's workspace role. Two channels plausibly match the vague descriptor, each with a different Robert as a genuine channel member, leaving the referent unresolved without further clarification.

task_spec.text: Determine which Robert is meant by identifying the channel where the team discusses AI model work and confirming his conversation membership there, then report that Robert's workspace membership role.

access_plan: Discover the population via conversations.list to enumerate channels and conversations.members on likely AI/model-related channels (engineering, model-research) to find members literally named Robert; cross-check with users.list/users.info for full names and user_teams-backed workspace role via users.info's workspace association. The ambiguity between the two Roberts must be surfaced back to the requester rather than silently resolved.
